page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128g-960s is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture. The server provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2.0 GHz. The processor features 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation. Local high-speed storage is bundled directly as a 960 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier single-threaded compute and compression throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance scored 3614.28, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 39.33 GB/sec, bzip3 single-threaded decompression delivered 17.52 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing measured 3022.0, all placing in the top 10%. Memory subsystem testing yielded a PassMark memory score of 2834.28 in the top 25%, with cached memory bandwidth reaching 1754.86 GB/sec. For lightweight inference, the system achieved 443.4 tokens/sec on 135M parameter model text generation and 2596.68 tokens/sec in prompt processing.

Multi-core execution and uncached memory throughput sit squarely in the middle 50% tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11603.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 34157.16. Large block uncached memory bandwidth registers at 88.87 GB/sec for reads and 45.5 GB/sec for writes. The hardware profile offers high resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring specialized accelerated hardware, though raw parallel scaling is constrained by the 8 physical core boundary.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation combined with dedicated NVMe storage makes this configuration appropriate for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, batch decompression pipelines, and memory-heavy backend application services.
